questions.answer: If you are like me, sports equipment will bankrupt you here.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out is cheaper than Cph. You can get a 0,5L beer for around 3,5-4 euros most bars and restaurants. The supermarkets are around the same price perhaps a bit cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Didn't use any offers from the host institution

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Skiing, climbing, hiking, mountain-biking, ice-skating, trail-running, via ferrata/klettersteig.. If you like being active you won't be bored here. The freizeitticket gives you access to almost all of the slopes in Tirol, including other stuff like ice-skating and all the cable cars. It's pretty expensive though, but if you plan to go skiing get it for sure.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Skiing, climbing, christmasmarket, hang out with other Erasmus students, go out and drink a lot of beers, go hiking etc. etc. etc. Lot's of stuff to do here :)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It's rather similar to danish culture. Tirol dialect is crazy though, good luck lol

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to the other german/austrian students who are also doing clinical rotations to get a friend group of locals besides all the international Erasmus people you meet here

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language (dialect is hard)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everyone is active and wants to do stuff outside

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Practice german as much as you can (listen to Easy German podcast all day)
Save a lot money for the trip (there are many expenses, if you need equipment like I did)
Talk german as much as you can, but don't be afraid to switch to english when it's needed, most people know some english

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You get coat and pants, but you have to bring your own t-shirt to the clinic

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: New friends across most of europe

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Language

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you want to learn a new language, get a bunch of international connections and enjoy skiing and other outdoor activities, you have to go! Time goes by so fast

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
